Regional Italian versus local language systems
Regional Italian is Italian shaped by local pronunciation, vocabulary and usage. Local languages traditionally called dialetti are not simply Italian spoken with an accent.

Many northern speakers prefer the passato prossimo in everyday accounts. The passato remoto remains more frequent in parts of the Centre and South, but choices also depend on time reference, genre and speaker.
Regional Italian has more than two uniform accents. Open and closed e/o, consonants and intonation vary across communities and individuals.
Words such as mica occur beyond their area of origin. Treat a regional tendency as a guide to recognition, not as a nationality or birthplace test.

Do not force a northern/southern rule onto every speaker. Passato remoto is not compulsory in the South, and passato prossimo is not prohibited there. Neapolitan and Sicilian need their own references; a generic Italian voice does not reproduce them.
